page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on KVM hypervisors. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. Cache sizing consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The instance includes 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and does not feature hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes present a distinct divide between single-threaded compute tasks and broader throughput benchmarks. In stress-ng single-core tests, the CPU registers in the top 25% of all tested systems. However, its multi-core capabilities, including the Geekbench multi-core score of 3400.0 and PassMark CPU score of 6182.79, fall into the bottom 25%, primarily constrained by the 4-vCPU hardware footprint. Memory throughput drops significantly when processing uncached structures, achieving 19.62 GB/sec for read and 13.66 GB/sec for write in 256 MB blocks, ranking in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7a.xlarge offers an economical footprint for applications needing high memory capacity relative to compute cores without paying for higher CPU allocations. However, applications requiring high parallel throughput or fast sequential uncached memory transfers will experience bottlenecks. Best-fit deployments include memory-intensive caching systems like Redis, moderate relational databases, background ETL processing, and small-scale memory-resident application backends.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, coupled with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB-per-vCPU ratio. The configuration features 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local storage, and no GPU hardware. Performance evaluation reveals strong single-core CPU execution, scoring in the upper quartile under stress-ng, while overall multi-threaded capacity and uncached memory bandwidth fall in the lower quartiles. This resource balance makes the server suitable for memory-intensive caching, light in-memory databases, and modest backend services.
